# Deliverable Package: Kaggle Google Gemma 4 Developer Agent — Representative Issues Compendium & Deep-Wide Research

*Folder: `deliverables/2026-11-05_Gemma4_Representative_Issues_Compendium_and_Deep_Research`*
*Baseline Taxonomy Referenced: `deliverables/2026-11-05_Gemma4_Problem_Dataset_Taxonomy_and_Analysis`*
*Source Dataset Analyzed: `input/kagglecomp/kagglecomp_data_package/` (`tasks.jsonl`, `HARNESS_README.md`, `gemma-4-developer-agent.zip`)*
*Date: 2026-11-05*

---

## 1. Executive Purpose & Deliverable Manifest

This deliverable package executes a comprehensive **Deep and Wide Research (`/rdw-deep-wide-research`)** investigation across every single category, sub-category, architectural subsystem, prompt solvability class, patch complexity tier, AST graph reachability class, runtime failure phenotype, and evolutionary multi-PR chain defined in [`deliverables/2026-11-05_Gemma4_Problem_Dataset_Taxonomy_and_Analysis`](file:///d:/stuff/ai-misc/_bsh2026/vscode_project01/101e-Kaggle-antigrav/deliverables/2026-11-05_Gemma4_Problem_Dataset_Taxonomy_and_Analysis/00_README.md) for the **Kaggle Google — The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Competition** ([https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent/data](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent/data)).

Across **106 distinct taxonomic groups** spanning all **6 orthogonal axes** (and 10 causal multi-PR chains) and covering **100% (129/129) of the public benchmark tasks**, this compendium provides:
1. **Complete Upstream GitHub Issue & PR Forensics**: Resolves every benchmark task (`#001`–`#129`) to its upstream GitHub Pull Request, release version, and linked GitHub Issue(s)—including complete recovery of the **29 opaque/issue-linked (`PC-5`) prompts** where the benchmark mined bare `Fixes https://github.com/.../issues/<N>` PR descriptions with empty `hints_text`.
2. **Deep-Dive Representative Issue Profiles**: For every category and sub-category, presents flagship benchmark issue profiles containing the exact problem statement, recovered upstream bug report context, code-level root-cause mechanism, unified diff (`patch`), verification test assertions (`test_patch`), 1-hop AST call-graph neighborhood (`graphs/*.json`), and actionable agent localization/repair playbooks.
3. **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Maps each category and sub-category to verified real-world issues across sibling Python repositories (`pydantic/pydantic`, `encode/starlette`, `litestar-org/litestar`, `pallets/flask`, `pallets/werkzeug`, `fastapi/typer`, `Textualize/textual`, `jquast/wcwidth`, `pallets/click`, `urllib3/urllib3`, `encode/httpcore`, `aio-libs/aiohttp`, and CPython `urllib`/`netrc`/`typing`) plus the project's **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards (`DC-01`–`DC-10`)** and **Strategic Rules (`SR-1`–`SR-8`)** to maximize transfer to the ~120 hidden private-repository evaluation tasks.

# Deep & Wide Research Synthesis: Representative Issues, Opaque Prompt Forensics & Cross-Ecosystem Parallels

**Scope:** Multi-angle empirical and external investigation of representative issues across all 106 taxonomic groups (6 Primary Categories, 17 Primary Sub-Categories, 8 Root-Cause Categories, 25 Root-Cause Sub-Categories, 18 Architectural Subsystems, 5 Prompt Specification Classes, 5 Patch Complexity Tiers, 4 AST Graph Reachability Classes, 8 Runtime Failure Modes, and 10 Evolutionary Multi-PR Chains) for the Kaggle Google Gemma 4 Developer Agent Competition (`129` public tasks across `fastapi/fastapi`, `Textualize/rich`, `psf/requests`, and `encode/httpx`, plus cross-ecosystem parallel issues across 12 sibling Python frameworks).
**As of:** 2026-11-05
**Baseline Taxonomy Referenced:** [`deliverables/2026-11-05_Gemma4_Problem_Dataset_Taxonomy_and_Analysis`](file:///d:/stuff/ai-misc/_bsh2026/vscode_project01/101e-Kaggle-antigrav/deliverables/2026-11-05_Gemma4_Problem_Dataset_Taxonomy_and_Analysis/00_README.md)

---

## Executive Summary

- **100% Upstream Issue & PR Forensics Across All 129 Tasks (`tasks.jsonl`):** Every task in the Gemma 4 Developer Agent public dataset corresponds to an authentic merged GitHub Pull Request (`fastapi` `#5077`–`#15800`, `rich` `#2725`–`#4079`, `requests` `#6589`–`#7505`, `httpx` `#3672`). However, because the benchmark construction pipeline extracted the **PR title and PR description body** rather than expanding linked GitHub Issue bodies (`hints_text` is empty `""` on 129/129 tasks), **29 tasks (`22.48%`, Class `PC-5`)** contain fewer than 180 characters—often just a 2–6 word title followed by `Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/<N>` [Source: `input/kagglecomp/kagglecomp_data_package/tasks.jsonl`]. Section 1 below provides the complete upstream forensic recovery for all 29 `PC-5` tasks.
- **Causal Multi-PR Chains & Exact Historical Reverts (`27/129` tasks, `20.93%`):** Deep forensic analysis of commit timelines and target lines reveals **10 multi-PR evolutionary chains (`CHAIN-01`–`CHAIN-10`)** where benchmark tasks directly extend, harden, or revert earlier benchmark tasks. Most notably, in `CHAIN-01`, `requests_6644` (2024-02-23) added two lines in `HTTPAdapter.request_url` to collapse leading double slashes (`//`) so `urllib3.util.parse_url('//v:h')` (`urllib3#3352`) would not misparse path segments as host/port authorities; two years later, `requests_7315` (2026-05-10, `requests 2.34.0`) **deleted those exact two lines** because collapsing `//` invalidated AWS S3 SigV4 presigned URLs (`requests#7431`) [Source: `tasks.jsonl` `#072`, `#077`; `src/requests/adapters.py`].
- **CPython 3.10–3.14 & Upstream Library Boundary Shifts Drive `26.36%` (`34/129`) of All Tasks:** Over a quarter of the benchmark stems from boundary friction with modern Python language features—PEP 604 `types.UnionType` (`fastapi_14430`), PEP 695 `typing.TypeAliasType` (`fastapi_13920`), PEP 563 `eval_str=True` + `if TYPE_CHECKING:` `NameError` (`fastapi_11355`, `fastapi_14485`), PEP 657 fine-grained tracebacks (`rich_3486`), PEP 678 `Exception.__notes__` (`rich_3676`), CPython 3.12's `typing._ProtocolMeta` switch from `hasattr` to `inspect.getattr_static` (`requests_7433`, `7502`, `7505`), CPython 3.11's `netrc` empty token tuples (`requests_7205`), and CPython `bpo-39057` `no_proxy` domain matching (`requests_7427`)—or major dependency transitions (`pydantic.v1` sunset `CHAIN-03`, Starlette 1.0 `on_event` removal `CHAIN-07`, `urllib3` 2.x `super_len` `requests_6757`).
- **FastAPI Executable Tutorial Coupling (`PC-4`, `10` tasks touching `docs_src/`):** In `fastapi/fastapi`, documentation examples under `docs_src/` are imported directly as Python modules by `tests/test_tutorial/`. Across 10 benchmark tasks (`9` in `PC-4` plus `fastapi_15280` in `PC-5`), Phase 2 evaluation (`test_patch`) executes `tests/test_tutorial/...` suites that fail with `ModuleNotFoundError` or `AssertionError` unless the agent creates or updates the exact `docs_src/<topic>/tutorial00X_py310.py` file alongside core `fastapi/` code [Source: `tasks.jsonl`; Section 2].
- **High Cross-Ecosystem Transferability to Private Evaluation Repositories:** Cross-checking every category and sub-category against 12 sibling Python repositories (`pydantic`, `starlette`, `litestar`, `flask`, `werkzeug`, `typer`, `textual`, `wcwidth`, `click`, `urllib3`, `httpcore`, `aiohttp`) and the empirical **BCF Brain Multi-Source Harvest (`DC-01`–`DC-10`, `SR-1`–`SR-8`)** confirms that **59.69% (`77/129`)** of tasks are single-file localized patches (`TIER-1` + `TIER-2`, $\le 35$ lines churn) governed by universal Python repair archetypes [Source: `deliverables/2026-10-13_BCF_Brain_MultiSource_Harvest_v2/brain/priors_summary.json`].

---

## 1. Upstream PR-Mining Forensics & Complete Resolution of the 29 Opaque (`PC-5`) Benchmark Prompts

In the Kaggle evaluation container (`network_mode="none"`), the Gemma 4 agent cannot query `github.com` to read external issue links. Yet **29 tasks (`22.48%` of the benchmark: 24 in `Textualize/rich`, 4 in `fastapi/fastapi`, and 1 in `psf/requests`)** fall into **Class `PC-5` (`Opaque / Ultra-Terse Prompt <180 chars`)**, where the PR author wrote a minimal title and `Fixes https://github.com/.../issues/<N>`. Table 1.1 resolves all 29 `PC-5` tasks to their upstream GitHub Issue, hidden bug symptom, and exact gold code fix.

| # | `instance_id` | Chars | Primary Sub-Category (`Axis 1B`) | Root-Cause (`Axis 2B`) | Raw Benchmark `problem_statement` (`tasks.jsonl`) | Linked Upstream GitHub Issue | Recovered Upstream Issue Context & Gold Repair Mechanism |
| ---: | :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 006 | `fastapi_15280` | 64 | `SUB-2A` | `RC-7A` | ✨ Add support for `@app.vibe()` ✨ Add support for `@app.vibe()` | FastAPI April 1st `@app.vibe()` Feature (PR #15280) | Adds `@app.vibe()` decorator method on `FastAPI` in `fastapi/applications.py` and creates `docs_src/vibe/tutorial001_py310.py`. Fix: Classic `PC-4` + `PC-5` trap: prompt is only 64 chars (`'✨ Add support for @app.vibe()'`), yet `tests/test_vibe.py` imports `docs_src.vibe.tutorial001_py310`. |
| 012 | `requests_7502` | 67 | `SUB-1A` | `RC-1B` | Fix `_encode_files` detection for `__getattr__`-based file wrappers | https://github.com/psf/requests/issues/7432 | Stage 2 of `CHAIN-02` (opaque `PC-5` prompt, 67 chars): `_encode_files` in `src/requests/models.py` checked `elif isinstance(fp, _SupportsRead):`, rejecting `__getattr__`-proxied file wrappers passed via `files=...`. Fix: Add `or hasattr(fp, 'read')` to `isinstance(fp, _SupportsRead)` in `PreparedRequest._encode_files`. |
| 020 | `rich_4077` | 66 | `SUB-2C` | `RC-7C` | proxy isatty Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/4041 | https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/4041 | Opaque `PC-5` prompt (`'proxy isatty / Fixes #4041'`). When `Live` wraps `sys.stdout` in `FileProxy`, calling `sys.stdout.isatty()` returned `False` because `FileProxy` did not delegate `isatty()` to `self.__file`. Fix: Add `def isatty(self) -> bool: return self.__file.isatty()` in `rich/file_proxy.py`. |
| 021 | `rich_4079` | 71 | `SUB-1E` | `RC-5B` | Inline table code Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/4038 | https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/4038 | Opaque `PC-5` prompt (`'Inline table code / Fixes #4038'`). Regression from `rich_3130`: `TableDataElement.on_text` in `rich/markdown.py` called `text.stylize(context.current_style)` on already-styled `Text` objects (such as inline code with `inline_code_lexer`), wiping out syntax highlight spans. Fix: Check `if isinstance(text, str): self.content.append(text, context.current_style) else: self.content.append_text(text)`. |
| 022 | `rich_4076` | 71 | `SUB-1E` | `RC-5C` | preserve newlines Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3577 | https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3577 | Opaque `PC-5` prompt (`'preserve newlines / Fixes #3577'`). `AnsiDecoder.decode` in `rich/ansi.py` used `terminal_text.splitlines()`, which strips trailing newlines (`'hello\n'` -> `'hello'`). Fix: Replace `terminal_text.splitlines()` with `re.split(r'(?<=\n)', terminal_text)` and strip `'\n'` per line. |
| 023 | `rich_4075` | 101 | `SUB-1E` | `RC-5C` | empty with end - Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3740 - Drop support for Python 3.8 | https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3740 | Opaque `PC-5` prompt (`'empty with end / Fixes #3740'`). Calling `console.print(end='!')` with no positional args unconditionally printed a newline (`objects = (NewLine(),)`) instead of respecting `end`. Fix: In `Console.print` (`rich/console.py`), set `objects = (NewLine(),) if end == '\n' else ('',)`. |

Fix: Pass a copy (`security_scopes=security_scopes.copy()` / list concatenation) when recursing into sub-dependencies in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`. |

Using `with console.capture():` on a `Console(record=True)` appended captured text into `self._record_buffer` even though `_buffer_index > 0`. Fix: Change `if self.record:` to `if self.record and not self._buffer_index:` in `Console._write_buffer` (`rich/console.py`). |
| 117 | `rich_3469` | 75 | `SUB-1E` | `RC-5C` | fix superfluous space Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3027 | https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3027 | Opaque `PC-5` prompt (`'fix superfluous space / Fixes #3027'`). Empty cells in a Markdown table caused `Markdown.__rich_console__` (`rich/markdown.py`) to emit extra blank lines above the table because `new_line` remained True on `'inline'` close tokens. Fix: Change `if new_line:` to `if new_line and node_type != 'inline':` in `rich/markdown.py`. |
| 127 | `rich_3064` | 76 | `SUB-1E` | `RC-5D` | fix for markdown table Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3053 | https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3053 | Opaque `PC-5` prompt (`'fix for markdown table / Fixes #3053'`). Rendering a partial/streaming Markdown table with no body rows raised `AssertionError` on `assert self.body is not None` in `TableElement.__rich_console__` (`rich/markdown.py`). Fix: Replace `assert self.header is not None` and `assert self.body is not None` with conditional `if` guards in `rich/markdown.py`. |
| 128 | `rich_3063` | 85 | `SUB-1E` | `RC-2B` | Fix escaping trailing backslash Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/2987 | https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/2987 | Opaque `PC-5` prompt (`'Fix escaping trailing backslash / Fixes #2987'`). `rich.markup.escape('foo\\')` did not escape a trailing backslash, which then escaped the `[` of a following closing markup tag (`[/red]`). Fix: In `rich/markup.py` (`escape`), append `'\\'` when `markup.endswith('\\') and not markup.endswith('\\\\')`. |

## 3. Python 3.10–3.14 Runtime & Upstream Dependency Boundary Shifts

A defining structural finding of our `/rdw-deep-wide-research` investigation is that **34 of the 129 benchmark tasks (`26.36%`)** are directly caused by behavioral shifts across Python 3.10–3.14 standard library internals or major upstream dependency releases (`Pydantic v2.12+`, `Starlette 0.48+/1.0`, `urllib3 2.x`). Table 3.1 synthesizes these 12 external boundary triggers and their benchmark manifestations.

| External Boundary Trigger (PEP / CPython / Upstream Release) | Technical Mechanism of Boundary Shift | Affected Benchmark Tasks (`tasks.jsonl`) | Taxonomic Coordinates (`Axis 1B` / `Axis 2B`) | Required Code-Level Adaptation Pattern |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CPython 3.12 `typing._ProtocolMeta.__instancecheck__`** | Python 3.12 switched `@runtime_checkable` `Protocol` `isinstance()` checks from `hasattr()` to `inspect.getattr_static()`, breaking proxy classes (`_TemporaryFileWrapper`, custom wrappers) that delegate `.read` or `.__iter__` dynamically via `__getattr__`. | `requests_7433`, `requests_7502`, `requests_7505` (`CHAIN-02`) | `SUB-1A`, `SUB-3C` / `RC-1B` | Replace or augment `@runtime_checkable` `Protocol` checks with explicit `hasattr(obj, 'read')` (`_t.has_read(obj)`) and `hasattr(data, '__iter__')`. |
| **Python 3.12 PEP 695 `type X = ...` (`typing.TypeAliasType`)** | PEP 695 `type` statements create lazy `typing.TypeAliasType` objects rather than eagerly expanding aliases at import time, causing `get_origin()` / `analyze_param()` to miss inner `Annotated` metadata. | `fastapi_13920` | `SUB-2B` / `RC-1A` | Check `is_typealiastype(annotation)` (via `typing_inspection.introspection`) and unwrap `annotation = annotation.__value__` before inspecting `Annotated`. |
| **Python 3.10 PEP 604 Union Syntax (`types.UnionType`)** | `X / Y` union syntax creates a `types.UnionType` whose `get_origin()` is `types.UnionType` rather than `typing.Union`, breaking legacy `origin_type is Union` checks. | `fastapi_14430` (extending `fastapi_14297`, `CHAIN-06`) | `SUB-1A` / `RC-1A` | Always check `if origin_type is Union or origin_type is UnionType:` (or `origin_type in (Union, UnionType)`). |
| **PEP 563 `from __future__ import annotations` + `inspect.signature(eval_str=True)`** | Evaluating stringified annotations at runtime via `eval_str=True` raises `NameError` when a parameter annotation references a symbol imported only inside an `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block; decorated functions also require `inspect.unwrap(call).__globals__`. | `fastapi_11355`, `fastapi_14485` (`CHAIN-05`), `fastapi_9425`, `fastapi_5077` | `SUB-1A`, `SUB-2B` / `RC-1C` | Wrap `inspect.signature(call, eval_str=True)` in `try ... except NameError:` falling back to `eval_str=False`, and evaluate forward refs against `inspect.unwrap(call).__globals__`. |
| **Python 3.11 PEP 657 Fine-Grained Error Locations in Bytecode** | Python 3.11+ frame instruction entries (`tb_lasti`) expose `co_positions()` 4-tuples `(lineno, end_lineno, col_offset, end_col_offset)` enabling column-accurate caret highlighting in tracebacks. | `rich_3486` | `SUB-2C` / `RC-7C` | Extract instruction position ranges in `Traceback.extract` (`rich/traceback.py`) and underline the exact expression span in `_render_stack`. |
| **Python 3.11 PEP 678 `BaseException.add_note()` (`__notes__`)** | Python 3.11+ allows attaching diagnostic strings in `exc.__notes__: list[str]`, which custom traceback formatters must explicitly render. | `rich_3676` | `SUB-2C` / `RC-7C` | Capture `getattr(exc_value, '__notes__', None)` into `Trace.notes` in `rich/traceback.py` and render `[bold]note:[/] ...` blocks after the exception message. |
| **CPython 3.11+ `netrc.netrc.authenticators()` Empty Tuple (`gh-104306`)** | When a `.netrc` entry contains only a `machine` token with no login/account/password, Python 3.11+ returns `('', '', '')` instead of raising `NetrcParseError`, causing `requests` to send empty Basic Auth `Authorization: Basic Og==`. | `requests_7205` | `SUB-1F` / `RC-2A` | Guard `if any(authenticators):` in `get_netrc_auth` (`src/requests/utils.py`) before returning `(authenticators[0], authenticators[2])`. |
| **CPython `urllib.request.proxy_bypass_environment` (`bpo-39057` / `gh-83238`)** | Suffix matching `host.endswith(no_proxy_item)` without a leading dot caused `no_proxy=ample.com` to erroneously bypass proxies for `example.com`. | `requests_7427` | `SUB-1F` / `RC-4B` | Require domain boundary matching (`host.endswith('.' + domain)`) when `no_proxy` entry does not start with `.`. |
| **Unicode 17.0 & UAX #29 Extended Grapheme Clusters (`jquast/wcwidth`)** | Multi-codepoint emoji sequences joined by U+200D (ZWJ), variation selectors (`VS15`/`VS16`), C0/C1 control codes, and Nerd Fonts Private Use Area (PUA) glyphs break single-codepoint `ord()` lookup tables. | `rich_3930`, `rich_3944`, `rich_3953`, `rich_4006` (`CHAIN-10`) | `SUB-2C`, `SUB-1D` / `RC-7A`, `RC-5A` | Versioned Unicode 4.1–17.0 grapheme tables + `split_graphemes()` with zero-width prefix step advance, C0/C1 width `0`, and PUA fallback width `1`. |
| **Pydantic v2.12+ & Python 3.14 `pydantic.v1` Deprecation & Removal** | Importing `pydantic.v1` on Python 3.14 emits ` Pydantic V1 functionality isn't compatible with Python 3.14`, requiring isolation and ultimate removal of FastAPI's v1 shim layer. | `fastapi_14186`, `fastapi_14583`, `fastapi_14605`, `fastapi_14609` (`CHAIN-03`) | `SUB-4A` / `RC-6A`, `RC-6B`, `RC-6C` | Isolate imports in `may_v1.py`, emit `FastAPIDeprecationWarning`, and remove all 20 v1 compatibility files (`-1,855` lines). |
| **Starlette 0.48+ (`HTTP_422`) & Starlette 1.0 (`on_event` Removal)** | Starlette 0.48 deprecated `HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` (RFC 9110 rename to `UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT`), and Starlette 1.0 scheduled removal of `on_startup`/`on_shutdown` routing lists. | `fastapi_14077`, `fastapi_14851`, `fastapi_14873` (`CHAIN-07`) | `SUB-4B`, `SUB-3A` / `RC-6B`, `RC-3C` | Use integer `422` directly and re-implement `_merge_lifespan_context` and `on_event` inside `fastapi/routing.py`. |
| **`urllib3` 1.26.x vs `urllib3` 2.x `Body` / `parse_url` Divergence** | `urllib3` 2.0 changed `str` body encoding in `httplib` (requiring UTF-8 byte length in `super_len`) while `urllib3` 1.26.x encoded strings as ISO-8859-1; `urllib3.util.parse_url('//v:h')` (`urllib3#3352`) also parsed leading `//` as authority. | `requests_6589`, `requests_6757`, `requests_6644`, `requests_7315` (`CHAIN-01`) | `SUB-1F`, `SUB-4B` / `RC-4B`, `RC-6B` | Gate UTF-8 `super_len` encoding on `is_urllib3_1` in `compat.py`; preserve raw `//` in `HTTPAdapter.request_url` for S3 SigV4 compatibility. |

## 4. Cross-Ecosystem Representative Issues Across 12 Sibling Python Repositories

Because the Kaggle competition's final evaluation runs on **~120 unseen tasks from private repositories**, an effective developer agent must recognize how the benchmark's categories and sub-categories manifest in other Python libraries. Table 4.1 maps the benchmark's core sub-categories to verified parallel issues across 12 sibling open-source repositories.

| Benchmark Sub-Category (`Axis 1B` / `Axis 2B`) | Benchmark Representative Issue(s) | Sibling Repository & Verified Parallel Issue / PR | Shared Architectural Mechanism & Transferable Repair Pattern |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`SUB-1A` / `RC-1A`**: Union, `Annotated` & `TypeAliasType` Unpacking | `fastapi_12942`, `fastapi_13920`, `fastapi_14512` | **`pydantic/pydantic` `#8998` & `#6352`**; **`litestar-org/litestar` `#5127` & PR `#3982`**; **`fastapi/typer` `#371`** | Recursive unwrapping of `typing.Annotated`, `typing.Union`, `types.UnionType`, and `typing.TypeAliasType` (`annotation.__value__`) before inspecting inner `FieldInfo` discriminators or scalar types. |
| **`SUB-1A` / `RC-1C`**: Stringified Annotations & `if TYPE_CHECKING:` | `fastapi_11355`, `fastapi_14485`, `fastapi_9425` | **`fastapi/typer` `#598`** (`from __future__ import annotations` with `Annotated`); **`pydantic/pydantic` `#9733`** (`eval_type_backport`) | Evaluating stringified annotations with `inspect.signature(call, eval_str=True)` while catching `NameError` when symbols exist only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` and passing `inspect.unwrap(call).__globals__`. |
| **`SUB-1B` / `RC-3A`**: Field Alias vs Attribute Name & `validation_alias` | `fastapi_15589`, `fastapi_14371`, `fastapi_13537` | **`pydantic/pydantic` `#10839` & `#9928`** (`validation_alias` / `AliasChoices` in `Annotated`) | Using a unified helper (`get_validation_alias(field)`) rather than assuming `field.alias == field.name`, and recording both raw and converted keys in `processed_keys`. |
| **`SUB-1B` / `RC-3B`**: `MultiDict.getlist()` vs Scalar JSON Extraction | `fastapi_14616`, `fastapi_14356`, `fastapi_14303` | **`pallets/werkzeug` & `pallets/flask` `MultiDict.getlist()`**; **`encode/starlette` `FormData`** | Extracting repeated keys via `.getlist()` for sequence types and `extra='allow'` models, while explicitly guarding `not _is_json_field(field)` so `Json[list[str]]` receives a single JSON string. |
| **`SUB-1C` / `RC-4A`**: OpenAPI 3.1 `$ref` & `@computed_field` Schema | `fastapi_14463`, `fastapi_14349`, `fastapi_13207` | **`pydantic/pydantic` `#5825`** (`@computed_field` schema); **`litestar-org/litestar` `#4682` & `#5049`** | Guarding `isinstance(v, str)` when traversing keys named `'$ref'`, deepcopying shared response dicts before mutating `anyOf`, and including `computed_fields` in serialization schemas. |
| **`SUB-1D` / `RC-5A`**: Unicode Grapheme Width & CJK Cell Splitting | `rich_4006`, `rich_3953`, `rich_3180`, `rich_3521` | **`Textualize/textual` `#4996` & `#5090`** (`Segment.split_cells`); **`jquast/wcwidth` `#104`** (UAX #29 grapheme widths) | Proportional byte-offset convergence in `Segment._split_cells`, zero-width grapheme prefix step advance (`end = max(end, index + 1)`), and double-width CJK overflow checks (`cell_len > max_width`). |
| **`SUB-1E` / `RC-8B`**: `BrokenPipeError` on Closed Stdout Pipe | `rich_3468` | **`pallets/click` `PacifyFlushWrapper`** (`click/utils.py`) | Catching `BrokenPipeError` during `Console.file.flush()`, redirecting `sys.stdout` to `os.devnull` to suppress secondary interpreter shutdown errors, and re-raising cleanly. |
| **`SUB-1F` / `RC-4B`**: RFC 9110 Header Parsing & `no_proxy` Boundaries | `requests_7427`, `requests_7309`, `requests_7315` | **`aio-libs/aiohttp` CVE-2025-69224** (header parser); **CPython `bpo-39057`** (`no_proxy`); **`urllib3/urllib3` `#3352`** | Enforcing leading `.` domain boundary checks on `no_proxy` suffixes, stripping whitespace around `;` parameters without dropping empty values, and preserving `//` in signed URI paths. |
| **`SUB-2A` / `RC-7A`**: Native Server-Sent Events (SSE) & Framing | `fastapi_15030`, `fastapi_15588` | **`sysid/sse-starlette` (`EventSourceResponse`)**; **`litestar-org/litestar` `#3772`** | Formatting `data:`/`event:`/`id:`/`retry:` lines with `\n` separation, running a 15s `: ping\n\n` keepalive task, and rejecting embedded `\r`/`\n` in `event` and `id` fields. |
| **`SUB-2A` / `RC-2A`**: Strict JSON `Content-Type` CSRF Enforcement | `fastapi_14978` | **`pallets/werkzeug` `#2550` / `Request.get_json()`** (`415 Unsupported Media Type`) | Checking `content_type` against `application/json` or `*+json` before parsing request bodies as JSON to block browser `text/plain` `fetch()` CSRF attacks. |
| **`SUB-2A` / `RC-8B`**: HTTP/1.1 Keep-Alive Request Stream Draining | `httpx_3672` | **`urllib3/urllib3` `HTTPResponse.drain_conn()`**; **` encode/httpcore` stream close**; **`aio-libs/aiohttp` `ClientResponse.release()`** | Draining unread request body bytes (`recv_body` / `arecv_body`) before resetting the HTTP/1.1 parser for the next keep-alive request on the same socket. |
| **`SUB-3A` / `RC-8B`**: Streaming Response Generator & Resource Teardown | `fastapi_14099` | **`pallets/flask` `#5774` (`stream_with_context`)**; **`litestar-org/litestar` `#3772`** | Splitting `AsyncExitStack` into an outer stack (closed when the endpoint returns) and an inner dependency stack wrapped inside `StreamingResponse` so `yield` dependencies stay open until streaming finishes. |

## 6. Open Questions & Private-Split Transfer Considerations

1. **Prevalence of `PC-5` Opaque Prompts in the Private Evaluation Split:** In the public dataset, `Textualize/rich` contributes 24 of the 29 `PC-5` tasks (`50.0%` of all `rich` tasks) due to the maintainer's habit of writing `Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/<N>` as the entire PR body. If the hidden private evaluation repositories use similar PR templates, the agent's ability to extract search tokens from a 3–6 word title (`SR-5`) and inspect recent git history (`git log -n 10 --stat`) will be the single highest-leverage determinant of localization recall.
2. **Executable Documentation Equivalents in Private Repositories:** While `docs_src/` is specific to Tiangolo repositories (`fastapi`, `typer`, `sqlmodel`), other Python frameworks test examples via `doctest` or `examples/` directories. Before finalizing any feature addition (`CAT-2`), the agent should run `rg` across `tests/` for references to `docs` or `examples`.

## 2. Primary Category `CAT-1: Functional Bug Fix & Edge-Case Resolution`

### 2.1. Comprehensive Category Summary

- **Taxonomic Definition & Engineering Scope**: Reactive defect resolution where existing library functionality crashes, raises an unintended exception (`TypeError`, `AttributeError`, `KeyError`, `NameError`, `RecursionError`, `AssertionError`), misparses protocol/schema inputs, or produces corrupted terminal/HTTP output on valid edge-case inputs.
- **Dataset Footprint**: **79 tasks** (`61.24%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `31`, `rich`: `38`, `requests`: `10`, `httpx`: `0`. Mean patch churn: `15.1` lines (median: `7` lines).
- **Constituent Sub-Categories**: `SUB-1A: Type Annotation, Union & Signature Introspection Bug`, `SUB-1B: Parameter Extraction, Aliasing & Form/Header/Query Coercion Bug`, `SUB-1C: OpenAPI / JSON Schema Generation & Ref Resolution Bug`, `SUB-1D: Terminal Cell Width, Unicode Grapheme & Segment Splitting Bug`, `SUB-1E: Terminal Component Rendering, Styling & Markup/ANSI Parsing Bug`, `SUB-1F: HTTP Protocol, URL/Header/Netrc Parsing & Lifecycle Bug`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Pydantic `#8998`/`#10839` (union/alias validation), Litestar `#5127` (`TypeAliasType`), CPython `bpo-39057` (`no_proxy`), Textual `#5090` (`Segment.split_cells`).
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: Declarative Cards `DC-01` (Type Coercion), `DC-02` (None/Attr Guard), `DC-04` (Boundary/Off-by-One), `DC-09` (Mutable State), `DC-10` (Dict Key Fallback); Strategic Rules `SR-1` (Repro Verify), `SR-7` (Localized Edit Focus).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_12942`, `fastapi_14485`, `fastapi_14463`, `requests_7433`, `requests_7427`, `rich_4006`, `rich_4079`, `rich_3772`.

### 2.2. Sub-Category `SUB-1A: Type Annotation, Union & Signature Introspection Bug` (14 Tasks, 10.85%)

- **Comprehensive Sub-Category Summary**: Defects in runtime inspection of Python type hints, `Annotated` metadata, PEP 604 `UnionType` (`A | B`), stringified forward references (`from __future__ import annotations`, `if TYPE_CHECKING:`), callable classes (`__call__`), `@functools.wraps` + `functools.partial` chains, `@dataclass` `init=False` fields, and `__getattr__`-proxied file wrappers.
- **Quantitative Profile**: **14 tasks** (`fastapi`: `9`, `rich`: `3`, `requests`: `2`, `httpx`: `0`); average `1.07` files and `2.07` hunks per patch; mean churn `18.6` lines (median `7` lines).
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Pydantic `#8998` & `#6352` (`TypeAliasType` + `Field`), Litestar `#5127` & PR `#3982` (`unwrap TypeAliasType`), Typer `#598` & `#371` (`from __future__ import annotations` + `UnionType`), CPython 3.12 `typing._ProtocolMeta` (`inspect.getattr_static`).
- **BCF Card & Rule Alignment**: `DC-01` (Type Coercion/Unwrapping), `DC-02` (Hasattr/None Guard), `RC-1A`/`RC-1B`/`RC-1C`.
- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_12942`, `fastapi_14512`, `fastapi_14485`, `fastapi_14448`, `requests_7433`, `rich_3894`.

#### Representative Issue Profile: `fastapi_12942` (`fastapi/fastapi` — 2025-10-08)

- **PR Title & Instance Metadata**: **🐛 Fix tagged discriminated union not recognized as body field** (`instance_id`: `fastapi_12942`, Base Commit: `27c0f7e75f`, Created: `2025-10-08`)
- **Upstream GitHub PR & Linked Issue(s)**: [PR `fastapi#12942`](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12942) | Upstream Reference: FastAPI Tagged Discriminated Union Body Recognition (PR #12942)
- **6-Axis Taxonomic Coordinates**:
  - **Axis 1 (Intent)**: `CAT-1: Functional Bug Fix & Edge-Case Resolution` $\rightarrow$ `SUB-1A: Type Annotation, Union & Signature Introspection Bug`
  - **Axis 2 (Root Cause)**: `RC-1: Type System, Introspection & Callable Unwrapping` $\rightarrow$ `RC-1A: Generic / Union / Annotated / TypeAliasType Unpacking`
  - **Axis 3 (Subsystem)**: `FastAPI-3: Pydantic Compatibility & Schema Adaptation (_compat/)`
  - **Axis 4 (Prompt Clarity)**: `PC-1` (1392 chars; `docs_src` coupled: `False`)
  - **Axis 5 (Complexity & Graph)**: `TIER-1` (`+3/-0` lines, 1 file(s), 1 hunk(s)) | `GRAPH-1`
  - **Axis 6 (Failure Phenotype)**: `FM-3: HTTP Status / Protocol Compliance Mismatch (401/403/422)`
- **Benchmark Problem Statement (`tasks.jsonl`)**:
  > 🐛 Fix tagged discriminated union not recognized as body field ## Problem When using a union type models with a tagged discriminator as an endpoint parameter, like the following: `py class Pie(BaseModel): time_to_cook: int num_ingredients: int class ApplePie(Pie): fruit: Literal["apple"] = "apple" class PumpkinPie(Pie): filling: Literal["pumpkin"] = "pumpkin" def get_discriminator_value(v: Any) -> str: if isinstanc...
- **Upstream Issue Forensics & Technical Root-Cause Mechanism**:
  A Pydantic v2 discriminated union (`Annotated[Union[Cat, Dog], Field(discriminator='pet_type')]`) has `origin is Annotated` or `Union` and was not recognized by `_is_complex_field` / `is_scalar_field` in `fastapi/_compat.py`, causing FastAPI to treat it as a query parameter instead of a JSON request body.
- **Target Files & Verification Test Suite**:
  - **Modified Source File(s)** (1): `fastapi/_compat.py`
  - **Verification `test_patch` File(s)** (1, `+188` lines): `tests/test_union_body_discriminator.py`

### 2.3. Sub-Category `SUB-1B: Parameter Extraction, Aliasing & Form/Header/Query Coercion Bug` (9 Tasks, 6.98%)

- **Comprehensive Sub-Category Summary**: Defects in extracting, coercing, and validating HTTP query, header, cookie, form, and multipart file parameters—specifically `field.alias` vs `field.name` mismatches, `convert_underscores=True` header leaks, `MultiDict.getlist()` vs scalar extraction (`Json[list[str]]`), empty HTML form strings (`''` -> `None`), and `Form`/`File` declaration order.
- **Quantitative Profile**: **9 tasks** (`fastapi`: `9`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `0`, `httpx`: `0`); average `1.33` files and `2.33` hunks per patch; mean churn `12.8` lines (median `7` lines).
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Pydantic `#10839` & `#9928` (`validation_alias` vs `alias` in `Annotated`), Werkzeug/Flask `MultiDict.getlist()` form/query coercion, Starlette `FormData` parsing.
- **BCF Card & Rule Alignment**: `DC-05` (Parameter Plumbing), `DC-10` (Key/Alias Lookup), `RC-3A`/`RC-3B`/`RC-3D`.
- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_15589`, `fastapi_14360`, `fastapi_14371`, `fastapi_14616`, `fastapi_11194`, `fastapi_14356`.

  Stage 1 of `CHAIN-01`: a request URL like `http://127.0.0.1:10000//v:h` produced path `//v:h`, which `urllib3.util.parse_url` treated as a schemeless authority (`host='v', port='h'`), crashing. `#6644` collapsed leading `//` via `url = f'/{url.lstrip("/")}'` (later reverted in `#7315`).

         url = request.path_url
+        if url.startswith("//"):  # Don't confuse urllib3
+            url = f"/{url.lstrip('/')}"
+
         if is_proxied_http_request and not using_socks_proxy:
             url = urldefragauth(request.url)
```

- **Agent Localization, Repair & Verification Playbook**:
  In `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`, import `is_typealiastype` from `typing_inspection.introspection` and unwrap `if is_typealiastype(annotation): annotation = annotation.__value__`.

```diff
--- a/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py
+++ b/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py
@@ -66,6 +66,7 @@

 from starlette.websockets import WebSocket

@@ -370,6 +371,9 @@ def analyze_param(

     type_annotation: Any = Any

+    if is_typealiastype(annotation):

## 4. Primary Category `CAT-3: Architectural Refactoring, Performance & Protocol Alignment`

### 4.1. Comprehensive Category Summary

- **Taxonomic Definition & Engineering Scope**: Internal structural reworks (`APIRouter` tree context preservation, `StreamingResponse` `AsyncExitStack` lifecycle, `Dependant` scope caching), fast-path execution optimizations (Pydantic v2 Rust `serialize_json`, deferred imports in `rich`), and RFC/security compliance alignments (RFC 9110 `401` vs `403`, OpenAPI 3.1 `contentMediaType`, SSE single-line validation).
- **Dataset Footprint**: **13 tasks** (`10.08%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `10`, `rich`: `2`, `requests`: `1`, `httpx`: `0`. Mean patch churn: `201.7` lines (median: `70` lines).
- **Constituent Sub-Categories**: `SUB-3A: Core Routing, Lifespan & Streaming Lifecycle Refactor`, `SUB-3B: Performance Optimization & Fast-Path Execution`, `SUB-3C: Standards, Security & Internal API Hygiene Refactor`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Flask `#5774` (`stream_with_context` async generator teardown), Litestar `#4682` (OpenAPI 3.1 binary schema), Werkzeug `#2550` (`Content-Type` enforcement).
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: Declarative Cards `DC-03` (Exception/Status Normalization), `DC-09` (State Isolation); Strategic Rules `SR-1` (Re-verify across dependent test suites), `SR-3` (70% Budget Fallback).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_15745`, `fastapi_14099`, `fastapi_14962`, `fastapi_13786`, `fastapi_15588`, `rich_4070`, `requests_7505`.

### 4.2. Sub-Category `SUB-3A: Core Routing, Lifespan & Streaming Lifecycle Refactor` (4 Tasks, 3.10%)

- **Comprehensive Sub-Category Summary**: Deep architectural refactorings of FastAPI's request/router lifecycle: preserving `APIRouter` and `APIRoute` instances via `_EffectiveRouteContext` instead of route cloning (`fastapi_15745`), keeping `yield` dependencies and `UploadFile`s alive until `StreamingResponse` completes (`fastapi_14099`), re-implementing `on_event` lifespans for Starlette 1.0 compatibility (`fastapi_14851`), and caching scopeless sub-dependencies (`fastapi_14419`).
- **Quantitative Profile**: **4 tasks** (`fastapi`: `4`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `0`, `httpx`: `0`); average `3.00` files and `11.50` hunks per patch; mean churn `481.5` lines (median `477` lines).
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Litestar `#3772` (SSE generator teardown), Flask `#5774` (`stream_with_context` async generator lifecycle), Starlette lifespan migration.
- **BCF Card & Rule Alignment**: `DC-09` (State/Context Isolation), `SR-1` (Multi-suite regression verification), `RC-3C`/`RC-6B`/`RC-8B`.
- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_15745`, `fastapi_14099`, `fastapi_14851`, `fastapi_14419`.

## 5. Primary Category `CAT-4: Ecosystem Compatibility, Deprecation & Legacy Removal`

### 5.1. Comprehensive Category Summary

- **Taxonomic Definition & Engineering Scope**: Lifecycle transitions managing upstream dependency shifts (`pydantic.v1` warning isolation, deprecation, and 20-file removal; Starlette 0.48+ `HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT`; `urllib3` 1.26.x vs 2.x `super_len` compatibility; `@deprecated` instrumentation on `ORJSONResponse`/`UJSONResponse`).
- **Dataset Footprint**: **7 tasks** (`5.43%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `6`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `1`, `httpx`: `0`. Mean patch churn: `365.6` lines (median: `44` lines).
- **Constituent Sub-Categories**: `SUB-4A: Pydantic v1 Deprecation & Removal Lifecycle`, `SUB-4B: Upstream Library Compatibility & Feature Deprecation`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Starlette `#2939` (RFC 9110 HTTP 422), Pydantic v2 migration shims (`pydantic.v1`), `urllib3` v1->v2 migration across `requests` and `botocore`.
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: Strategic Rules `SR-4` (Strict Tracked File Hygiene during multi-file deletions), `SR-5` (Wide `rg` search to catch all deprecated call sites).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_14609`, `fastapi_14186`, `fastapi_14605`, `fastapi_14964`, `fastapi_14077`, `requests_6757`.

### 5.2. Sub-Category `SUB-4A: Pydantic v1 Deprecation & Removal Lifecycle` (4 Tasks, 3.10%)

- **Comprehensive Sub-Category Summary**: The complete 4-stage sunset (`CHAIN-03`) of `pydantic.v1` in FastAPI between October and December 2025: isolating `may_v1.py` imports for Python 3.14 (`fastapi_14186`), emitting `DeprecationWarning` on v1 models (`fastapi_14583`), introducing `FastAPIDeprecationWarning(UserWarning)` (`fastapi_14605`), and removing `pydantic.v1` support across 20 files (`fastapi_14609`, `-1,855` lines).
- **Quantitative Profile**: **4 tasks** (`fastapi`: `4`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `0`, `httpx`: `0`); average `9.75` files and `42.25` hunks per patch; mean churn `619.8` lines (median `364` lines).
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Pydantic v2.12+ / Python 3.14 compatibility removal of `pydantic.v1`, LangChain/SQLModel v1->v2 shim removal.
- **BCF Card & Rule Alignment**: `RC-6A`/`RC-6B`/`RC-6C`, `SR-5` (Exhaustive `rg pydantic\.v1` sweep across `/workspace`).
- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_14609`, `fastapi_14186`, `fastapi_14605`, `fastapi_14583`.

- **Upstream Issue Forensics & Technical Root-Cause Mechanism**:

## 2. Root-Cause Category `RC-1: Type System, Introspection & Callable Unwrapping`

### 2.1. Comprehensive Root-Cause Category Summary

- **Defect & Modification Mechanism**: Defects and extensions in Python runtime type inspection and callable unwrapping (22 tasks, 17.05%): unpacking `Annotated`, `Union`, PEP 604 `UnionType` (`A | B`), and PEP 695 `TypeAliasType`; evaluating stringified annotations (`eval_str=True`, `if TYPE_CHECKING:` `NameError`, `-> None`); and unwrapping `@functools.wraps`, `functools.partial`, callable classes (`__call__`), `@dataclass` fields, and `__getattr__` proxy objects.
- **Dataset Footprint**: **22 tasks** (`17.05%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `15`, `rich`: `3`, `requests`: `4`, `httpx`: `0`. Mean patch churn: `15.1` lines (median: `7` lines).
- **Constituent Root-Cause Sub-Categories**: `RC-1A: Generic / Union / Annotated / TypeAliasType Unpacking`, `RC-1B: Callable / Decorator / Partial / Class Unwrapping & Protocol Check`, `RC-1C: Stringified / Forward Reference & Signature Evaluation`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: CPython 3.12 `typing._ProtocolMeta` (`inspect.getattr_static`), Pydantic `#8998`/`#6352`, Litestar `#5127`, Typer `#598`.
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: `DC-01` (Type Coercion & Unwrapping), `DC-02` (Hasattr/None Guard).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_12942`, `fastapi_13920`, `fastapi_14485`, `fastapi_14448`, `requests_7505`, `requests_7433`, `rich_3894`.

- **Upstream Issue Forensics & Technical Root-Cause Mechanism**:
  A Pydantic v2 discriminated union (`Annotated[Union[Cat, Dog], Field(discriminator='pet_type')]`) has `origin is Annotated` or `Union` and was not recognized by `_is_complex_field` / `is_scalar_field` in `fastapi/_compat.py`, causing FastAPI to treat it as a query parameter instead of a JSON request body.
- **Target Files & Verification Test Suite**:
  - **Modified Source File(s)** (1): `fastapi/_compat.py`
  - **Verification `test_patch` File(s)** (1, `+188` lines): `tests/test_union_body_discriminator.py`
  - **Verification Test Function(s)**: `test_discriminator_pydantic_v2`

  - **Indexed Target Node(s)**: `fastapi._compat.field_annotation_is_complex`
  - **1-Hop Core Callers (`in_edges`)**: `fastapi._compat._annotation_is_complex`, `fastapi._compat.field_annotation_is_complex`, `fastapi._compat.field_annotation_is_scalar`
  - **1-Hop Test Callers (`tests.*`)**: *None indexed directly*
  - **1-Hop Callees (`out_edges`)**: `fastapi._compat.field_annotation_is_complex`, `fastapi._compat._annotation_is_complex`, `fastapi._compat.field_annotation_is_scalar`
- **Agent Localization, Repair & Verification Playbook**:
  Unwrap `Annotated` in `is_scalar_field` (`fastapi/_compat.py`) and return `False` when `get_origin(field.type_) is Union`.

```diff
--- a/fastapi/_compat.py
+++ b/fastapi/_compat.py
@@ -590,6 +590,9 @@ def field_annotation_is_complex(annotation: Union[Type[Any], None]) -> bool:
     if origin is Union or origin is UnionType:

+    if origin is Annotated:
+        return field_annotation_is_complex(get_args(annotation)[0])
+
     return (
         _annotation_is_complex(annotation)
         or _annotation_is_complex(origin)
```

### 2.3. Root-Cause Sub-Category `RC-1B: Callable / Decorator / Partial / Class Unwrapping & Protocol Check` (11 Tasks, 8.53%)

- **Comprehensive Mechanism Summary**: Unwrapping decorated callables (`inspect.unwrap`), `functools.partial` (`_impartial`), callable classes (`inspect.isclass` vs `__call__`), custom `__eq__` on default params (`is` vs `==`), uninitialized `@dataclass` fields (`hasattr`), unusual `__qualname__` descriptors, `JSONDecodeError.__reduce__` MRO, and `__getattr__`-proxied file wrappers failing Python 3.12 `@runtime_checkable` `Protocol` `isinstance()` checks.
- **Quantitative Profile**: **11 tasks** (`fastapi`: `4`, `rich`: `3`, `requests`: `4`, `httpx`: `0`); average `1.18` files and `2.00` hunks per patch; mean churn `17.1` lines (median `7` lines).

## 3. Root-Cause Category `RC-2: Input Validation, Sanitization & Boundary Guard`

### 3.1. Comprehensive Root-Cause Category Summary

- **Defect & Modification Mechanism**: Missing protocol/format boundary validation, control-character/newline/escape-sequence sanitization, and cycle/self-reference guards (12 tasks, 9.30%): SSE single-line validation, `strict_content_type` JSON CSRF checking, `netrc` empty token validation, `Authorization` header `.strip()`, ANSI/markup escaping, router self-inclusion guard, and cyclic exception `Traceback` guard.
- **Dataset Footprint**: **12 tasks** (`9.30%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `7`, `rich`: `4`, `requests`: `1`, `httpx`: `0`. Mean patch churn: `28.1` lines (median: `4` lines).
- **Constituent Root-Cause Sub-Categories**: `RC-2A: Missing Protocol / Format Boundary Validation`, `RC-2B: Escaping, Stripping & Control-Code Sanitization`, `RC-2C: Self-Reference / Cycle Guard & Diagnostic Assertion`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Werkzeug `#2550` (`415` JSON `Content-Type`), CPython `netrc` `gh-104306`, Python 3.11 `traceback` `_seen` cycle set.
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: `DC-02` (Boundary Guard), `DC-03` (Exception Normalization), `DC-04` (Boundary Condition).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_15588`, `fastapi_14978`, `requests_7205`, `fastapi_14986`, `rich_3063`, `fastapi_14258`, `rich_3772`.

### 3.2. Root-Cause Sub-Category `RC-2A: Missing Protocol / Format Boundary Validation` (3 Tasks, 2.33%)

- **Comprehensive Mechanism Summary**: Enforcing strict protocol boundary invariants before processing or emitting data: rejecting `\r`/`\n` in SSE `event`/`id` fields (`fastapi_15588`), validating `application/json` `Content-Type` headers when `strict_content_type=True` (`fastapi_14978`), and rejecting empty `('', '', '')` `netrc` authenticator tuples (`requests_7205`).
- **Quantitative Profile**: **3 tasks** (`fastapi`: `2`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `1`, `httpx`: `0`); average `1.67` files and `5.67` hunks per patch; mean churn `35.7` lines (median `23` lines).
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Werkzeug `#2550` (`415 Unsupported Media Type` on missing JSON `Content-Type`), CPython `gh-104306` (`netrc`).
- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_15588`, `fastapi_14978`, `requests_7205`.

## 4. Root-Cause Category `RC-3: Data Structure, State & Dictionary Key / Alias Mapping`

### 4.1. Comprehensive Root-Cause Category Summary

- **Defect & Modification Mechanism**: Defects in dictionary key/alias mapping, multi-value container extraction, mutable state sharing, and parameter forwarding (23 tasks, 17.83%): `field.alias` vs `field.name` lookups, `MultiDict.getlist()` vs `Json[list[str]]`, shallow-copy dict/list mutation (`copy.deepcopy`, `.copy()`), stale cached hashes (`_hash = None`), and missing keyword forwarding across call chains.
- **Dataset Footprint**: **23 tasks** (`17.83%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `17`, `rich`: `5`, `requests`: `1`, `httpx`: `0`. Mean patch churn: `67.8` lines (median: `5` lines).
- **Constituent Root-Cause Sub-Categories**: `RC-3A: Alias vs Field Name Key Lookup / Set Tracking Defect`, `RC-3B: MultiDict / Sequence / Extra Parameter Aggregation Defect`, `RC-3C: Mutable State Sharing, Shallow Copy & Cache Pollution`, `RC-3D: Missing Parameter / Option Forwarding Across Call Chain`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Pydantic `#10839` (`validation_alias`), Werkzeug `MultiDict.getlist()`, SWE-rebench mutable state (`DC-09`, `DC-10`).
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: `DC-05` (Parameter Plumbing), `DC-09` (Mutable Default / State Isolation), `DC-10` (Dict Key Fallback).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_15589`, `fastapi_14371`, `fastapi_14616`, `fastapi_14463`, `requests_7328`, `rich_3480`, `rich_2943`, `fastapi_14301`.

### 4.2. Root-Cause Sub-Category `RC-3A: Alias vs Field Name Key Lookup / Set Tracking Defect` (4 Tasks, 3.10%)

- **Comprehensive Mechanism Summary**: Resolving mismatches between Python attribute names (`field.name`), Pydantic aliases (`field.alias`), and `validation_alias` (`get_validation_alias(field)`) when extracting query/header/cookie parameters, tracking `processed_keys` for `convert_underscores=True`, and coercing empty HTML form strings (`''` -> `None`).

- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Pydantic `#10839` & `#9928` (`validation_alias` vs `alias` resolution).
- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_15589`, `fastapi_14360`, `fastapi_14371`, `fastapi_13537`.

## 5. Root-Cause Category `RC-4: Schema, Protocol & Specification Alignment`

### 5.1. Comprehensive Root-Cause Category Summary

- **Defect & Modification Mechanism**: Mismatches between library output/parsing and external specifications (OpenAPI 3.1, JSON Schema 2020-12, RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics, RFC 8470 Early Data, AWS SigV4 URL signing, CPython `bpo-39057` `no_proxy`, SPDX license IDs; 18 tasks, 13.95%).
- **Dataset Footprint**: **18 tasks** (`13.95%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `12`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `6`, `httpx`: `0`. Mean patch churn: `28.1` lines (median: `12` lines).
- **Constituent Root-Cause Sub-Categories**: `RC-4A: OpenAPI / JSON Schema Structure & $ref Remapping`, `RC-4B: HTTP / URL / Header / Status / Auth RFC Compliance`, `RC-4C: Documentation Example / Constant Specification Fix`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: CPython `bpo-39057` (`no_proxy`), `urllib3#3352` (`//` path parsing), Starlette `#2939` (RFC 9110 HTTP 422), Litestar `#4682` (OpenAPI 3.1).
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: `DC-04` (Delimiter/Domain Boundary), `DC-10` (`'$ref' in schema` Guard).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_14349`, `fastapi_13207`, `fastapi_14953`, `fastapi_13786`, `requests_7427`, `requests_7315`, `requests_7309`, `requests_6592`.

### 5.2. Root-Cause Sub-Category `RC-4A: OpenAPI / JSON Schema Structure & $ref Remapping` (8 Tasks, 6.20%)

- **Comprehensive Mechanism Summary**: Aligning generated JSON Schemas and OpenAPI 3.1 documents with specification rules: guarding `isinstance(v, str)` on fields literally named `'$ref'` (`fastapi_14349`), checking `'$ref' in schema` (`fastapi_14361`), including `@computed_field` when `separate_input_output_schemas=False` (`fastapi_13207`), separating nested input/output schemas (`fastapi_14246`), deduplicating OAuth2 security schemes (`fastapi_14455`), propagating top-level security schemes (`fastapi_14266`), adding `input`/`ctx` to `ValidationError` (`fastapi_14791`), and using `contentMediaType: application/octet-stream` for `bytes` (`fastapi_14953`).
- **Quantitative Profile**: **8 tasks** (`fastapi`: `8`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `0`, `httpx`: `0`); average `1.38` files and `1.88` hunks per patch; mean churn `24.1` lines (median `14` lines).
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Pydantic `#5825` (`@computed_field`), Litestar `#4682` & `#5049` (OpenAPI 3.1 schema generation).
- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_14349`, `fastapi_13207`, `fastapi_14246`, `fastapi_14953`, `fastapi_14455`, `fastapi_14791`.

### 5.3. Root-Cause Sub-Category `RC-4B: HTTP / URL / Header / Status / Auth RFC Compliance` (8 Tasks, 6.20%)

## 7. Root-Cause Category `RC-6: Ecosystem Compatibility, Deprecation & Legacy Cleanup`

### 7.1. Comprehensive Root-Cause Category Summary

- **Defect & Modification Mechanism**: Cross-version compatibility, deprecation warnings, and dead-code removal across upstream library transitions (8 tasks, 6.20%): `@deprecated` and `FastAPIDeprecationWarning`, `pydantic.v1` isolation and 20-file removal, Starlette 0.48+ status codes, `APIRouter` `on_event` re-implementation, and `urllib3` 1.26.x vs 2.x compatibility.
- **Dataset Footprint**: **8 tasks** (`6.20%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `7`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `1`, `httpx`: `0`. Mean patch churn: `339.5` lines (median: `52` lines).
- **Constituent Root-Cause Sub-Categories**: `RC-6A: Deprecation Warning & Decorator Instrumentation`, `RC-6B: Upstream Dependency API Migration (Pydantic v2 / Starlette / urllib3)`, `RC-6C: Legacy Compatibility Layer & Dead-Code Removal`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: Starlette `#2939`, Pydantic v2 migration shims, `urllib3` v1/v2 compatibility in `botocore`/`requests`.
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: `SR-4` (Patch Hygiene), `SR-5` (Wide `rg` search across all call sites).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_14609`, `fastapi_14186`, `fastapi_14605`, `fastapi_14964`, `fastapi_14851`, `requests_6757`.

### 7.2. Root-Cause Sub-Category `RC-6A: Deprecation Warning & Decorator Instrumentation` (3 Tasks, 2.33%)

- **Comprehensive Mechanism Summary**: Instrumenting deprecated APIs with user-visible warnings and PEP 702 `@deprecated` decorators: introducing `FastAPIDeprecationWarning(UserWarning)` (`fastapi_14605`), emitting warnings when `pydantic.v1` models are used (`fastapi_14583`), and deprecating `ORJSONResponse`/`UJSONResponse` (`fastapi_14964`).
- **Quantitative Profile**: **3 tasks** (`fastapi`: `3`, `rich`: `0`, `requests`: `0`, `httpx`: `0`); average `3.33` files and `9.33` hunks per patch; mean churn `40.0` lines (median `44` lines).
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: PEP 702 (`warnings.deprecated` / `typing_extensions.deprecated`) and custom `UserWarning` subclasses.
- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_14605`, `fastapi_14583`, `fastapi_14964`.

+

## 9. Root-Cause Category `RC-8: Performance & Resource Lifecycle Optimization`

### 9.1. Comprehensive Root-Cause Category Summary

- **Defect & Modification Mechanism**: Throughput/startup fast-paths and deterministic resource cleanup (6 tasks, 4.65%): Pydantic v2 Rust `serialize_json` fast-path (`fastapi_14962`), deferred imports in `rich` (`rich_4070`), `AsyncExitStack` teardown after `StreamingResponse` (`fastapi_14099`), `with read_image():` stream context manager (`fastapi_15023`), `BrokenPipeError` devnull redirect (`rich_3468`), and HTTP/1.1 keep-alive request body draining (`httpx_3672`).
- **Dataset Footprint**: **6 tasks** (`4.65%` of benchmark) — `fastapi`: `3`, `rich`: `2`, `requests`: `0`, `httpx`: `1`. Mean patch churn: `134.5` lines (median: `79` lines).
- **Constituent Root-Cause Sub-Categories**: `RC-8A: Serialization Fast-Path & Deferred Import Optimization`, `RC-8B: Context Manager / Stream / Pipe Resource Cleanup`.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Parallel Representative Issues**: `urllib3` `drain_conn()`, `aiohttp` `ClientResponse.release()`, Click `PacifyFlushWrapper`, Flask `#5774`.
- **BCF Declarative Pattern Cards & Strategic Rules**: `SR-1` (Lifecycle & performance verification), `SR-5` (Dual-tree sync/async check in `httpx_3672`).
- **Category Flagship Representative Issues**: `fastapi_14962`, `rich_4070`, `fastapi_14099`, `httpx_3672`, `rich_3468`, `fastapi_15023`.

- **Comprehensive Mechanism Summary**: Eliminating hot-path serialization overhead and cold-start import latency: Pydantic v2 Rust `serialize_json` fast-path (`fastapi_14962`) and lazy/deferred module imports across 9 files in `Textualize/rich` (`rich_4070`).
- **Quantitative Profile**: **2 tasks** (`fastapi`: `1`, `rich`: `1`, `requests`: `0`, `httpx`: `0`); average `6.00` files and `19.50` hunks per patch; mean churn `91.5` lines (median `128` lines).

- **Flagship Benchmark Representative Issues**: `fastapi_14099`, `httpx_3672`, `rich_3468`, `fastapi_15023`.

- **Benchmark Problem Statement (`tasks.jsonl`)**:
  > Server connection handling. * Add `HTTPParser.keep_alive`. * Server... always read request to completion on keep alives. * `HTTPParser.complete` -> `.reset` * Close streams on server exit. * Don't raise `KeyboardException` on server exit.
- **Upstream Issue Forensics & Technical Root-Cause Mechanism**:
  In the dual sync (`src/httpx/`) and async (`src/ahttpx/`) HTTP/1.1 parser/pool/server implementation, returning a response before consuming the request stream left unread request body bytes in the socket buffer, corrupting the next keep-alive request.
- **Target Files & Verification Test Suite**:

  - **1-Hop Callees (`out_edges`)**: `ahttpx._parsers.HTTPParser`, `ahttpx._parsers.ReadAheadParser`

  A Pydantic v2 discriminated union (`Annotated[Union[Cat, Dog], Field(discriminator='pet_type')]`) has `origin is Annotated` or `Union` and was not recognized by `_is_complex_field` / `is_scalar_field` in `fastapi/_compat.py`, causing FastAPI to treat it as a query parameter instead of a JSON request body.
- **Target Files & Verification Test Suite**:

- **Agent Localization, Repair & Verification Playbook**:
  Unwrap `Annotated` in `is_scalar_field` (`fastapi/_compat.py`) and return `False` when `get_origin(field.type_) is Union`.

```diff
--- a/fastapi/_compat.py
+++ b/fastapi/_compat.py
@@ -590,6 +590,9 @@ def field_annotation_is_complex(annotation: Union[Type[Any], None]) -> bool:
     if origin is Union or origin is UnionType:
         return any(field_annotation_is_complex(arg) for arg in get_args(annotation))
 
+    if origin is Annotated:
+        return field_annotation_is_complex(get_args(annotation)[0])
+
     return (
         _annotation_is_complex(annotation)
         or _annotation_is_complex(origin)

- **Benchmark Problem Statement (`tasks.jsonl`)**:
  > 🐛 Fix OpenAPI duplication of `anyOf` refs for app-level responses with specified `content` and `model` as `Union` ## Summary Fixes an issue where defining app-level `responses={...}` with a `Union` of Pydantic models **and** specifying `["content"][...]["examples"]` causes the generated OpenAPI schema to accumulate duplicate `$ref` entries in the `anyOf` array. ## Minimal reproducible example <details open> <summa...
- **Upstream Issue Forensics & Technical Root-Cause Mechanism**:
  When app-level `responses={400: {'model': Union[ErrorA, ErrorB], 'content': {'application/json': {}}}}` was shared across multiple routes, shallow-copying the response dict mutated the inner `'content'` dict in-place on each route, appending duplicate `{'$ref': ...}` items to `anyOf`.

  - **1-Hop Core Callers (`in_edges`)**: `fastapi.utils.is_body_allowed_for_status_code`, `fastapi.utils.deep_dict_update`, `fastapi._compat.shared.lenient_issubclass`, `fastapi._compat.v2.get_schema_from_model_field`
  - **1-Hop Test Callers (`tests.*`)**: *None indexed directly*
  - **1-Hop Callees (`out_edges`)**: `fastapi.openapi.utils.get_openapi_operation_metadata`, `fastapi.dependencies.utils.get_flat_dependant`, `fastapi.openapi.utils.get_openapi_security_definitions`, `fastapi.openapi.utils._get_openapi_operation_parameters`

  Replace `.copy()` with `copy.deepcopy()` when cloning response metadata in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`.

@@ -377,7 +378,7 @@ def get_openapi_path(

- **Benchmark Problem Statement (`tasks.jsonl`)**:
  > Fix #6628 - JSONDecodeError are not deserializable See issue #6628 for full bug-report ----- requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError are not deserializable: calling `pickle.dumps` followed by `pickle.loads` will trigger an error. This is particularly a problem in a process pool, as an attempt to decode json on an invalid json document will result in the entire process pool crashing. This is due to the MRO of the `requ...
- **Upstream Issue Forensics & Technical Root-Cause Mechanism**:
  `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError` inherits from `(InvalidJSONError, CompatJSONDecodeError)`. Because `InvalidJSONError -> RequestException -> IOError` comes first in MRO, pickling across `multiprocessing` called `IOError.__reduce__` (1 arg) instead of `CompatJSONDecodeError.__reduce__` (3 args: `msg, doc, pos`), crashing process pools.
- **Target Files & Verification Test Suite**:
  - **Modified Source File(s)** (1): `src/requests/exceptions.py`
  - **Verification `test_patch` File(s)** (1, `+10` lines): `tests/test_requests.py`
  - **Verification Test Function(s)**: `test_json_decode_errors_are_serializable_deserializable`
- **AST Call-Graph & Embedding Neighborhood (`requests_7a13c041dbef42f9f3feb14110f02626f6892e9a.json`, 712 nodes / 1,750 edges)**:
  - **Indexed Target Node(s)**: `requests.exceptions.RequestException.__init__`, `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError.__init__`, `requests.exceptions.HTTPError`
  - **1-Hop Core Callers (`in_edges`)**: `requests.exceptions.RequestException`, `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError`, `requests.models.Response.ok`, `requests.models.Response.raise_for_status`
  - **1-Hop Test Callers (`tests.*`)**: `tests.test_requests.test_http_error`
  - **1-Hop Callees (`out_edges`)**: `requests.exceptions.RequestException`, `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError`, `tests.test_requests.test_http_error`, `requests.models.Response.ok`
- **Agent Localization, Repair & Verification Playbook**:
  Define `def __reduce__(self): return CompatJSONDecodeError.__reduce__(self)` on `JSONDecodeError` in `src/requests/exceptions.py`.

```diff
--- a/src/requests/exceptions.py
+++ b/src/requests/exceptions.py
@@ -41,6 +41,16 @@ def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
         CompatJSONDecodeError.__init__(self, *args)
         InvalidJSONError.__init__(self, *self.args, **kwargs)
 
+    def __reduce__(self):
+        """
+        The __reduce__ method called when pickling the object must
+        be the one from the JSONDecodeError (be it json/simplejson)
+        as it expects all the arguments for instantiation, not just
+        one like the IOError, and the MRO would by default call the
+        __reduce__ method from the IOError due to the inheritance order.
+        """
+        return CompatJSONDecodeError.__reduce__(self)
+
 
 class HTTPError(RequestException):
     """An HTTP error occurred."""
```

- **Upstream Issue Forensics & Technical Root-Cause Mechanism**:
  When a Pydantic model is used with `Header(convert_underscores=True)` and `extra='allow'`, sending raw underscore headers (e.g. `x_token`) alongside hyphenated headers caused the raw underscore header to leak into `extra` fields because only the hyphenated alias was added to `processed_keys`.

  - **Indexed Target Node(s)**: `fastapi.dependencies.utils.request_params_to_args`

  - **1-Hop Test Callers (`tests.*`)**: *None indexed directly*
  - **1-Hop Callees (`out_edges`)**: `fastapi._compat.shared.lenient_issubclass`, `fastapi._compat.v2.get_cached_model_fields`, `fastapi.dependencies.utils._get_multidict_value`, `fastapi.dependencies.utils._validate_value_with_model_field`
- **Agent Localization, Repair & Verification Playbook**:
  In `request_params_to_args` (`fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`), mark both the converted header name and `get_validation_alias(field)` in `processed_keys`.

```diff
--- a/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py
+++ b/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py
@@ -826,6 +826,10 @@ def request_params_to_args(
         if value is not None:
             params_to_process[get_validation_alias(field)] = value
         processed_keys.add(alias or get_validation_alias(field))
+        # For headers with convert_underscores=True, mark both the converted
+        # header name and the original field alias as processed to avoid
+        # accepting the original alias as an extra header.
+        processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))
 
     for key in received_params.keys():
         if key not in processed_keys:

+

+    match = re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+", version)

Strings starting with zero-width characters (`'\x1b'`, `'\ufe0f'`, `'\u200d'`) caused `split_graphemes()` in `rich/cells.py` to skip indices or fail to record a span when `spans` was empty, hanging `chop_cells()` in an infinite loop.

Two years later, `requests_7315` (2026-05-10, fixing `#7431` in `requests 2.34.0`) **deleted those exact two lines** because collapsing `//` mutated canonical URI paths on AWS S3 presigned URLs whose object keys started with `/` or contained `//`, causing S3 to reject requests with `403 Forbidden (SignatureDoesNotMatch)`.

### 5.3. `CHAIN-02`: Python 3.12+ `@runtime_checkable` `Protocol` & `__getattr__` File-Wrapper Detection Trilogy (`psf/requests`)

- **Causal Chain Narrative**: Triggered by Issue `#7432` and CPython 3.12's change to `typing._ProtocolMeta.__instancecheck__` (using `inspect.getattr_static` instead of `hasattr`), file-like wrappers that delegate `.read` and `.__iter__` via `__getattr__` (such as `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` / `_TemporaryFileWrapper`) failed `isinstance(data, Iterable)` and `isinstance(fp, SupportsRead)`. `requests_7433` added `or hasattr(data, '__iter__')` in `prepare_body`; `requests_7502` added `or hasattr(fp, 'read')` in `_encode_files`; and `requests_7505` extracted `def has_read(obj)` into `src/requests/_types.py` and applied it across `_encode_params`, `_encode_files`, and `prepare_body`.
